evals.name: checkpoints
evals.prompt: I want to add checkpoints like Conductor's, so that code and chat can be rolled back to an earlier turn. Look at how they did it and tell me how we should implement it.
evals.expected_output: Explains Conductor's checkpoint mechanism from the bundled script — a private git ref, non-disruptive save, temp index for untracked files — labels the evidence, states octopus has none, and turns it into an implementation direction rather than an essay.
assertions: Names the private ref refs/conductor-checkpoints/<id> as where a checkpoint is stored
States that saving moves neither HEAD nor any file on disk
Describes the second/temporary index used to capture untracked files
Labels which claims come from the bundled script versus the docs versus inference
States that octopus has no checkpoints today
Proposes a concrete direction for octopus rather than only describing Conductor

evals.name: env-files
evals.prompt: When a new workspace is created it has no .env and will not start. How does Conductor solve this?
evals.expected_output: Identifies Files to copy / .worktreeinclude, gives the resolution order, notes only gitignored files are eligible, separates it from a setup script, and says octopus lacks the feature.
assertions: Gives the resolution order: .worktreeinclude, then file_include_globs, then the default .env* pattern
States that only files git already ignores are eligible
Distinguishes copying static files from running a setup script
States that octopus has no equivalent today

evals.name: non-goal-guard
evals.prompt: In Conductor you can pick Codex or Cursor instead of Claude Code. Let's do the same here: look at how their agent choice is built and plan it for us.
evals.expected_output: Answers factually how Conductor's harnesses work, but surfaces that multi-agent support is a recorded non-goal in docs/PROJECT.md §5 and §6 before planning anything — then leaves the decision to the user instead of silently building or flatly refusing.
assertions: Identifies multi-agent support as a declared non-goal, citing docs/PROJECT.md
Still answers factually how Conductor runs four harnesses
Names the concrete architectural cost for octopus, such as the direct Agent SDK integration in agent.ts
Puts the decision back to the user rather than either refusing outright or planning as if nothing were at stake
